title: Zowie Expands AI Customer-Service Agents into Romania
summary:
The Polish AI firm is opening a Bucharest office, backed by $20m in prior funding, targeting banks, telecoms and insurers in a low-adoption market.
The post Zowie Expands AI Customer-Service Agents into Romania appeared first on The Fintech Times.
content: Polish artificial intelligence firm Zowie is expanding its AI customer-service agents into Romania by opening a new office in Bucharest. Backed by $20 million in previous funding, the company aims to target banks, telecommunications companies, and insurers in a market that currently has low adoption of AI technology.
content_ta: போலந்து நாட்டைச் சேர்ந்த AI நிறுவனமான Zowie, Bucharest நகரில் புதிய அலுவலகத்தைத் திறப்பதன் மூலம் தனது AI வாடிக்கையாளர் சேவை முகவர்களை ருமாலியாவில் விரிவுபடுத்துகிறது. இதற்கு முன்பு பெறப்பட்ட $20 மில்லியன் நிதியுதவியுடன், குறைந்த அளவு AI தொழில்நுட்ப பயன்பாடு உள்ள இச்சந்தையில் உள்ள வங்கிகள், தொலைத்தொடர்பு நிறுவனங்கள் மற்றும் காப்பீட்டு நிறுவனங்களை இந்நிறுவனம் குறிக்கோளாகக் கொண்டுள்ளது.

Mastercard Opens Its Largest Innovation Centre of Excellence in Asia Pacific to Drive the Intelligence Economy
summary:
Mastercard today opened its largest Innovation Centre of Excellence (ICoE)  in Asia Pacific, creating a new regional hub where financial institutions, merchants, governments and  technology partners can work alongside Mastercard specialists to shape the future of commerce in the  intelligence economy. 
The 7,200+ sq L facility brings together expertise in AI, cybersecurity, customer experience and rapid  prototyping, turning promising ideas into real-world solutions faster. More than 55 specialists are already  working across the ICoE to help partners address emerging challenges, strengthen resilience and create  better digital experiences.  
Mastercard plans to add over 250 specialist roles in Singapore by the end of 2029, expanding the talent and  capabilities needed to advance responsible AI, trusted digital commerce, cybersecurity, data and payments  across the region. 
“Mastercard's Innovation Centre of Excellence brings together banks, merchants, technology companies and  governments to develop and test new solutions. By combining expertise in AI, cybersecurity and fraud intelligence, it will help turn emerging technologies into solutions that businesses and consumers can trust,”  said Dr Tan See Leng, Minister for Energy, Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry), Singapore, at the  launch. “I hope the ICoE will become a lighthouse for payments innovation in Asia Pacific, where new  solutions are developed and proven in Singapore, before being adapted and deployed across ASEAN, India  and beyond.” 
“Mastercard’s Innovation Centre of Excellence marks a new chapter in our long-standing and mul4-faceted  partnership. By deepening its capabilities in AI, cybersecurity and threat intelligence, Mastercard will tackle  emerging challenges and seize new opportunities across Asia Pacific. Singapore will continue to be a key hub  where companies like Mastercard can innovate and pioneer the next generation of technologies for global  markets, and create high-value jobs for Singaporeans,” said Png Cheong Boon, Chairman, Singapore  Economic Development Board (EDB). 
Bringing together the capabilities to build what’s next 
Designed to evolve with changing technologies, risks and business models, the ICoE brings four  complementary spaces together in one facility: 
• AI Centre of Excellence: advancing responsible AI solutions that can make commerce safer, smarter  and more intuitive, including applications in agency commerce, fraud and scam prevention. • Fusion Centre: bringing together experts across cyber, fraud and physical security to identify  emerging risks, coordinate response efforts and strengthen resilience across the ecosystem. • Mastercard Experience Centre: giving financial institutions, merchants and public sector partners an  immersive way to explore emerging technologies and new possibilities for their businesses. • Makerspace: providing a hands-on environment to rapidly prototype, test and refine ideas,  shortening the journey from concept to reality. 
“Singapore continues to distinguish itself through its ambition, talent and ability to stay ahead of change.  Mastercard has been proud to grow its presence here. This new investment reflects our confidence in  Singapore’s future and Mastercard’s commitment to being a partner for the long term,” said Jon Huntsman,  Vice Chairman and President, Strategic Growth, Mastercard. 
“Asia Pacific is moving quickly into a more intelligent and interconnected economy. The opportunity is to turn  new technology into real-world value, securely and at scale,” said Richard Wormald, President, Asia Pacific,  Mastercard. “The ICoE builds on Mastercard’s longstanding collaboration with EDB and Singapore’s strength  as a proven testbed for innovation. It unites capabilities that traditionally sat apart, supporting the region in tackling shared challenges and moving promising ideas into practice faster.” 
From Singapore, shaping the future of commerce across Asia Pacific 
The opening of ICoE in Singapore comes as businesses across Asia Pacific look to close the gap between  technology experimentation and adoption. By 2030, more than one in 10 online shoppers are projected to  routinely use AI agents to make purchases on their behalf, while US$3 trillion to US$5 trillion in global  consumer commerce could be influenced or orchestrated by agency AI. Realizing this opportunity will  require businesses to deploy new technologies responsibly, with security, governance and human oversight  built in from the outset, particularly in a region where cybercrime already accounts for over 30% of recorded  crime. 
The ICoE will connect Mastercard expertise and insights across more than 40 Asia Pacific markets. From  Singapore, it will develop solutions for the region’s diverse needs, with the potential for the strongest ideas  to scale globally.

content: Mastercard has opened its largest Innovation Centre of Excellence in Asia Pacific, based in Singapore. The facility unites expertise in AI, cybersecurity, customer experience, and rapid prototyping to shape the future of digital commerce. Mastercard plans to add over 250 specialist roles in Singapore by the end of 2029 to support advanced technology solutions across the region.
content_ta: Asia Pacific பகுதியில் தனது மிகப்பெரிய Innovation Centre of Excellence மையத்தை Singapore நாட்டில் Mastercard திறந்துள்ளது. டிஜிட்டல் வர்த்தகத்தின் எதிர்காலத்தை வடிவமைப்பதற்காக AI, சைபர் பாதுகாப்பு மற்றும் வாடிக்கையாளர் அனுபவம் சார்ந்த நிபுணத்துவத்தை இந்த மையம் ஒருங்கிணைக்கிறது. இப்பகுதியில் மேம்பட்ட தொழில்நுட்ப தீர்வுகளை ஆதரிக்க 2029 இறுதிக்குள் Singapore நாட்டில் 250-க்கும் மேற்பட்ட நிபுணர் பணியிடங்களை சேர்க்க Mastercard திட்டமிட்டுள்ளது.
